⚔️ August 6 – the heroic defense of the Osowiec Fortress – a memorable date in Russia's military history.

#OTD, 1️⃣1️⃣1️⃣ years ago, Russian soldiers carried out one of the most extraordinary counterattacks of World War I.

At around 4 am on August 6, 1915, German forces, which had been laying siege to Osowiec Fortress for months, launched a massive poison-gas attack against its Russian garrison. 

The defenders had no effective protection, and the gas devastated the garrison and turned the battlefield into a poisoned wasteland.

Believing the fortress silenced, thousands of German troops advanced. Instead, they were met by several dozen surviving Russian soldiers of the 13th Company, led by Second Lieutenant Vladimir Kotlinsky.

Their faces covered with blood-soaked cloth, the poisoned defenders emerged from the trenches and charged with fixed bayonets.

🏳️ The sight broke the German advance. The attackers panicked, fled and became entangled in their own barbed wire as the surviving Russian artillery opened fire. The lost positions were retaken.

This counterattack entered history as the Attack of the Dead Men – an enduring symbol of the Russian soldier’s courage, devotion to duty and indomitable spirit.
